title: Base change in the fixed-point square
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, and let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible
cohomological correspondence with
fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$, so that the
fixed square of
[prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian] is Cartesian.

1. *Pullback along the ordinary leg.* For
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$,
$$
Li_F^*Lc_2^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ld^*K,
$$
the functoriality of the
derived pullback along
the equality $c_2i_F=d$.
1. *Base change for the total correspondence.* For
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$,
$$
L\Delta_X^*Rc_!M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rd_!Li_F^*M,
$$
the
compact-support base change of the
six-operations package in the Cartesian fixed square. For
$N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, its right-adjoint form (from the
compatibility of the exchange with the adjunction data of
[def-trf-admissibility]) is
$$
Rc^!R\Delta_{X*}N\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Ri_{F*}Rd^!N.
$$

proof.text: Check the geometric hypotheses of the operation package. By [def-trf-correspondence], $X$ and $C$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Put $Y=X\times_sX$. The projection $Y\to X$ is the base change of $X\to s$, hence separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Composition of separated and locally finite-type morphisms is [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e); quasi-compactness of $Y$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2). Thus $Y$ is separated finite type over $k$. For any $k$-map $v:T\to U$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](f) to $T\to U\to s$ to obtain local finite type; apply [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](b) to obtain separatedness. Separatedness of $U$ implies quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $v$ quasi-compact; hence it is finite type. Apply this to $c:C\to Y$, $\Delta_X:X\to Y$, and $c_2:C\to X$. The square in [prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian] now makes $d$ a base change of $c$ and $i_F$ a base change of $\Delta_X$. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $d:F\to X$ and $i_F:F\to C$ are separated finite type. In particular $d$ is locally of finite type and quasi-compact; compose $d$ with $X\to s$. Clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] gives separatedness and local finite type of $F\to s$, and clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $F$ quasi-compact since $X$ is quasi-compact. Thus $F$ is separated finite type over $k$, so the four corners and all four arrows satisfy the package hypotheses.

proof.text: At $A=A_{E,n}$, use the constant-coefficient derived pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The maps of constant ring sheaves in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] send each constant section $a$ to $a$. The direct and successive identifications therefore agree on constants and on sections glued from their clopen fibres; uniqueness in the sheafification construction makes the coefficient identification for the composite the composite of the identifications. Thus the ring identifications meet the composition theorem’s hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] with $h=i_F$ and $k=c_2$, and invert its composition comparison. Since $c_2i_F=d$ by [prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian], its value at $K$ is the natural isomorphism $Li_F^*Lc_2^*K\simeq L(c_2i_F)^*K=Ld^*K$. This proves the ordinary-leg assertion, with the specified derived pullback rather than an exceptional inverse image.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and displayed pullback-composition equation; Stacks 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition

proof.text: In the Cartesian square of [prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian], substitute $(f,g,f',g')=(c,\Delta_X,d,i_F)$ into clause (4) of [prop-functor-package]. Step 1 checks the scheme hypotheses; $A_{E,n}$ with $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ is its finite coefficient stage, and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$ is in its stated bounded finite-Tor domain. Its compact-support comparison, the exchange transformation defined in [def-exchange-projection], gives a natural isomorphism $\alpha:L\Delta_X^*Rc_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rd_!Li_F^*$. Evaluating at $M$ proves the compact-support assertion. Invertibility is taken from the theorem [prop-functor-package], not from the definition of the transformation.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: compact-support exchange with f=c, g=diagonal, f′=d, g′=i_F

proof.text: Set $P_1=L\Delta_X^*Rc_!$ and $P_2=Rd_!Li_F^*$. The finite-stage exceptional adjunctions and their constructible domains are supplied by [prop-functor-package], in the notation of [def-trf-admissibility]. Clause (1) of [fix-prop-adjunctions] supplies the ordinary adjunctions $L\Delta_X^*\dashv R\Delta_{X*}$ and $Li_F^*\dashv Ri_{F*}$. The pullbacks and direct images preserve $D^b_{ctf}$ by the finite-stage domain assertions of [prop-functor-package]. Because $D^b_{ctf}$ is a full subcategory of $D^b_c$, the ordinary adjunction Hom bijections for objects in $D^b_{ctf}$ have the same Hom sets, so they restrict to adjunctions on $D^b_{ctf}$ with the same units and counits. Compose the adjunctions using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Explicitly, for $M\in D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$ and $N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ the two composites of Hom bijections are $\operatorname{Hom}(P_1M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rc_!M,R\Delta_{X*}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,Rc^!R\Delta_{X*}N)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(P_2M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Li_F^*M,Rd^!N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,Ri_{F*}Rd^!N)$. Thus $P_1\dashv Q_1=Rc^!R\Delta_{X*}$ and $P_2\dashv Q_2=Ri_{F*}Rd^!$ with their pasted units and counits. These are constructible adjunctions, so no unrestricted ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint is needed.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: identification of the two right adjoints; Stacks 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits

proof.text: Write $\eta_j,\varepsilon_j$ for the composite adjunction data of step 4. Apply [lem-trf-adjoint-mate] to the natural isomorphism $\alpha:P_1\xrightarrow{\sim}P_2$ from step 3. It gives the natural isomorphism $\beta:Q_1\to Q_2$ with $\beta=(Q_2\varepsilon_1)\circ(Q_2\alpha^{-1}Q_1)\circ(\eta_2Q_1)$ and inverse $(Q_1\varepsilon_2)\circ(Q_1\alpha Q_2)\circ(\eta_1Q_2)$. The lemma also states both unit and counit compatibility and uniqueness. Consequently this is the specified right-adjoint comparison; the inverse of $\alpha$ in the formula accounts for its direction. Evaluation at $N$ gives $Rc^!R\Delta_{X*}N\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_{F*}Rd^!N$, the final assertion.

No new nodes. Second reading makes the fixed-scheme finite-type check and full-subcategory restriction of ordinary adjunctions explicit.
split_report.blueprint: Main 20261015 proof paragraph 1 is step 2; paragraph 2 is steps 3–5; step 1 verifies the scheme hypotheses of that paragraph.

tool_uses.why: The source explicitly applies clause (4) for compact-support base change, and its finite-stage constructible adjunction/domain assertions; these generic six-operation tools are not proved inside the diagonal trace-class unit.
Only clause (1), the ordinary pullback/direct-image adjunction, is used to form the two composite adjunctions; its stronger ambient exceptional hypothesis in clause (2) is not invoked.
Generic ringed pro-etale derived-pullback composition for the ordinary leg, explicitly required by the source; this unit supplies the equality of maps, not that general functoriality theorem.

Generic uniqueness, invertibility, and unit/counit compatibility for right adjoints of isomorphic left adjoints; it formalizes the source’s final mate argument without replacing any geometric trace-class route.

Its canonical constant-section-preserving ring-sheaf identifications give the coefficient maps for applying general ringed pro-etale pullback composition; it is a generic coefficient tool, not another trace-class argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-52da04f1b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item with all 5 steps and all 16 cited node statements, including the main-20261015 blueprint_update versions. The statement is verbatim the main-20261015 statement (order 2658) and the master statement (order 2314): finite A_{E,n}, D^b_ctf on the pro-étale site, base change from package clause (4) with (f,g,f',g')=(c,Delta_X,d,i_F) in the Cartesian square of prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian. Two inferences are compressed but elementary: T is quasi-compact, and U is quasi-separated via clause (2). Step 2: 0D6D (sites-cohomology l.3658); the composite ring identification agrees with c^{kh}_A because both preserve constant sections, and the direction is correct. Step 3: invertibility comes from prop-functor-package (4) on D^b_ctf, not from def-exchange-projection, which explicitly asserts none. Step 5: lem-trf-adjoint-mate gives beta:Q1->Q2 via alpha^{-1}. This is the inverse of the def-trf-admissibility conjugate, and all three citers use this same orientation.
